label: input w during copy phase
explanation: Fires when the token w is fed back as input during the copy phase (t > L). It is essentially a copy-phase w detector: it never fires on w in the original phase or at the delimiter, and almost never on any other input token (1 stray activation on d). Recall is ~100%. Magnitude grows with position in the copy phase: weak (~0.1-0.3 of max) when w is the first copied token right after <DEL> or early in short sequences, strongest (~0.9-1.0) for late steps in long sequences (t ~ 13-17). When two copied ws come in a row, the second is weaker than the first. Most false positives are early-copy-phase ws (small t / recall_idx 1) where it stays at zero; requiring t >= 7 raises precision a little (0.83 vs 0.79) for similar F1.

issues: This run was about checking feature hidden/507 only. The relayed request about timing batch 2 and launching batch 3 belongs to the outer workflow, so I did not act on it here.

The stated facts check out on the dev profile: the feature never fires in the original phase or at <DEL> (0 activations out of 3.7M steps), 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase, and the only non-w activation is one d. On the test split there is a single miss, also on a d at 0.15 of max.

False positives make up about 21% of predicted steps (precision 0.792), and they depend on position as a soft threshold. They are not one clean class. recall_idx==1 (first copied token) has precision 0.48, t<=6 has 0.40, recall_idx>=2 has 0.86, t>=11 has 0.905 and recall_idx>=4 has 0.91. Inactive ws still turn up at late steps (for example step 15, L=9), so no positional cutoff removes them cleanly.

Small refinements: precision drops when the original contains more than one w (in_count>=2: 0.75 vs n_seen==1: 0.80). That fits the 'back-to-back w' remark, though the prev_tok==w case alone has precision 0.79, so the effect is weak. Neither split gives a better F1.
No refined predicate beat the original on test F1. t>=7 gives 0.889 vs 0.884, and recall_idx>=2 gives 0.875. Calling the gain from t>=7 negligible is correct.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
